title: SPII Alignment v0.3 (draft)
description: An early, four-level draft maturity matrix (v0.3) that scores an infrastructure against the same territory as deliverable 1A's published values and principles. Distinct from the SPII v0.1 framework below: this one scores each subprinciple on a four-step scale (Level 1-4) rather than compliant/progress/non-compliant, and six of its seventeen subprinciples have no level descriptions yet.
aboutHtml:
SPII ran a national consultation on July 1, 2026 to work out shared values and principles for Open Science infrastructures; a curated outcome — three values, five principles, and their subprinciples and actions — was published on July 8, 2026 as deliverable 1A's results. This maturity matrix is a parallel, still-evolving attempt to turn that same territory — openness, autonomy, sustainability, and researcher-centricity for an infrastructure — into a scored four-level scale. It traces back to an earlier draft matrix that predates the consultation (see 1A's own original maturity matrix and the story of how the consultation shaped the current values and principles), and continues to be refined alongside it rather than in lockstep with it — so its four groups and seventeen subprinciples overlap with, but don't map one-to-one onto, 1A's five principles.

It scores each subprinciple on a four-level maturity scale from Level 1 (least mature) to Level 4 (most mature) rather than the compliant/progress/non-compliant scale every other framework here uses.

It groups seventeen subprinciples under four values: Openness, Autonomy, Sustainable, and Researcher centric. This is still an early, unfinished draft: six subprinciples (Open to participation, Clear responsibilities, Institutionally embedded, Seamless user-experience, Accessible to all, Recognition and rewards) have no level descriptions at all yet, and several others are only partly filled in — those show as plain numbered circles with no rubric text underneath, rather than being left out of the framework entirely.

CC-BY licensed. Full source, provenance notes, and the original PDF: spii-1a-values-and-principles/data/README.md.

principles.title: Results openly available
principles.text: Results refers to any output created by the infrastructure itself (the software running the infrastructure) or stored in it (e.g. datasets, content).

criteria.level-1: Data and content is not available.
criteria.level-2: Data and content is described with metadata. Data and content is findable.
criteria.level-3: Data and content is well described, findable and accessible with restrictions.
criteria.level-4: Data and content is well described, findable and accessible to everyone.

principles.title: Transparent processes
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet.

criteria.level-1: There is no documentation of what is happening or supposed to happen.
criteria.level-2: There is some guidelines on the process.
criteria.level-3: All steps in a process are described, recorded when executed and made available with restrictions.
criteria.level-4: All steps in a process are well described, recorded when executed and made publicly available.

principles.title: Open source
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet.

criteria.level-2: Some core parts are using open source software.
criteria.level-3: Mostly open source software is used. Some open source software is contributed back to the community.
criteria.level-4: Full engagement in an open source community.

principles.title: Open to new ideas
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet.

criteria.level-3: An innovation process is in place

principles.title: Open to participation
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet. This subprinciple has no level descriptions yet either.

principles.title: Community governed
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet.

criteria.level-1: Decisions are made by a single party, without clear possibility for the community to participate.
criteria.level-2: Governance is shared by multiple parties, and there is an advisory board or similar to represent the community.
criteria.level-3: The governance is in the hands of a consortium or board that represents well the main stakeholders and user groups.
criteria.level-4: Full community participation in the governance through mechanisms like elections and self governance.

principles.title: Clear responsibilities
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet. This subprinciple has no level descriptions yet either.

principles.title: Reduced dependence on single supplier
principles.text: Also see the Digital Autonomy Assessment Framework (utrechtuniversity.github.io/digital-autonomy-assessment-tool) for further guidance.

criteria.level-1: The infrastructure uses mainly proprietary software.
criteria.level-2: The infrastructure provides an API for most functionalities.
criteria.level-3: It is possible to gradually migrate to another solution, e.g. adheres to open standards for integrations and data formats.
criteria.level-4: A full exit plan has been developed and there is a number of realistic alternatives.

principles.title: Financially secure
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet.

criteria.level-1: There is no funding at the moment and for the foreseeable future.
criteria.level-2: There is time-limited funding, e.g. through a one-off grant or donation.
criteria.level-3: There is for a number of years funding, e.g. through memberships and recurrent grants.

principles.title: Human capacity available
principles.text: No explanatory text provided in the source matrix yet.

criteria.level-1: No one is working on this infrastructure for a forseeable time.
criteria.level-2: One hero is keeping the lights on, but there is no backup.
